neet_che_u06_t06_1.working: A catalyst speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally. It leaves K and the equilibrium position unchanged and only shortens the time taken to reach equilibrium.

neet_che_u06_t06_2.working: At constant pressure, adding argon increases the volume and lowers the partial pressures. The equilibrium shifts toward more gas moles (Δn = +1), i.e. forward, so dissociation of N2O4 increases. K is unchanged.

neet_che_u06_t06_4.working: Δn(gas) = 0, so pressure has no effect and A is true. NO formation is endothermic, so R is true. However, R concerns temperature and does not explain the pressure behaviour in A.

neet_che_u06_t06_5.working: Compression increases the NH3 yield, but K depends only on temperature, so I is incorrect. Inert gas at constant volume leaves partial pressures unchanged, so there is no shift and II is correct.
